title: Defining Relative Clauses in Context
grammarNote:
Определительные (Defining) и неопределительные (Non-defining) клаузы:

🔵 DEFINING — обязательная информация:
Без неё предложение теряет смысл. БЕЗ запятых. "That" возможен.
"The student who answered first got bonus points."
(Какой студент? — WHO ANSWERED FIRST. Убери — непонятно!)

🟡 NON-DEFINING — дополнительная информация:
Можно убрать. ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО с запятыми. "That" НЕЛЬЗЯ!
"My professor, who teaches linguistics, is brilliant."
(Убери: "My professor is brilliant." ✅ — всё понятно)
"The Eiffel Tower, which was built in 1889, attracts tourists."

💡 Тест:
Если убрать → непонятно → Defining (без запятых)
Если убрать → понятно → Non-defining (с запятыми)

⚠️ "That" ТОЛЬКО в Defining:
"The book that I need is out of stock." ✅
"War and Peace, that was written by Tolstoy..." ❌ (нужно "which")

grammarExtra.title: Omitting the relative pronoun (defining clauses only)

rows.form: The film (that) I watched was incredible.
The book (which) she recommended is out of stock.
The student (who) we met is from Astana.
The story (that) he told was fascinating.
She is the teacher (who) I admire most.
That's the film (that) everyone is watching.
❌ The Kite Runner that is a novel is my favourite.
rows.example: ✅ The Kite Runner, which is a novel, is my favourite.

rows.form: ❌ Amir who studies engineering won the award.
rows.example: ✅ Amir, who studies engineering, won the award.

rows.form: ❌ The film, that I watched, was amazing.
rows.example: ✅ The film that I watched was amazing. (no commas)

rows.form: ❌ Kamila, that loves books, is a blogger.
rows.example: ✅ Kamila, who loves books, is a blogger.

rows.form: ❌ The student loves reading won the award.
rows.example: ✅ The student who loves reading won the award.

rows.form: ❌ Dr. Akhmetov who teaches at WKU wrote a book.
rows.example: ✅ Dr. Akhmetov, who teaches at WKU, wrote a book.

grammarTip:
Простой тест — убери клаузу:

"The woman [who called you] is my aunt."
Убери: "The woman is my aunt." → НЕПОНЯТНО (какая?)
→ DEFINING (без запятых) ✅

"Aizhan, [who called you], is my aunt."
Убери: "Aizhan is my aunt." → ПОНЯТНО (и так ясно кто)
→ NON-DEFINING (с запятыми) ✅

📌 Три отличия:
Defining: без запятых · "That" можно · убрать нельзя
Non-defining: с запятыми · "That" нельзя · убрать можно

exercises.text: "The book ___ I borrowed is on the table." Defining or non-defining?
exercises.hint: No specific name given — "the book" needs to be identified → defining, no commas.

exercises.text: "The Kite Runner, ___ is set in Afghanistan, is my favourite book." Fill in:
exercises.hint: Non-defining clause for a thing → "which" (with commas).

exercises.text: Which sentence is a non-defining relative clause?
opts: The film that I watched was great.
She is the student who always asks questions.
Amir, who studies engineering, won the award.
I need a book that challenges me.
exercises.correct: Amir, who studies engineering, won the award.
exercises.hint: "Amir, who studies engineering, won." — commas + extra info = non-defining.

exercises.text: "That" can be used in non-defining relative clauses.
exercises.hint: "that" is NEVER used in non-defining clauses. Use "who" or "which" instead.

exercises.text: Dr. Akhmetov, ___ teaches English at WKU, is very inspiring.
exercises.hint: Non-defining clause for a person → "who" (with commas).

exercises.text: In "The book (that) she recommended is out of stock," why can "that" be omitted?
opts: Because it's the object of the clause
Because it refers to a place
exercises.correct: Because it's the object of the clause
exercises.hint: Object pronouns can be omitted in defining clauses. Subject pronouns cannot.

exercises.text: Foundation, ___ was written by Asimov, is a classic of science fiction.
exercises.hint: Non-defining clause for a thing → "which" (with commas).
Non-defining relative clauses are always separated from the main clause by commas.

exercises.text: "Kamila ___ loves reading is a blogger." Should this be defining or non-defining?
opts: Defining — she is identified by loving reading
Non-defining — her name already identifies her
exercises.correct: Non-defining — her name already identifies her
exercises.hint: When a name is used, the person is already identified → non-defining (commas).

exercises.text: WKU, ___ is located in Uralsk, offers a modern English programme.

opts: Zhibek that is the club president loves documentaries.
Zhibek, who is the club president, loves documentaries.
Zhibek, that is the club president, loves documentaries.
Zhibek who is the club president, loves documentaries.
exercises.correct: Zhibek, who is the club president, loves documentaries.

exercises.text: In a defining relative clause, "who/that" can be omitted when it is the object.
exercises.hint: Object pronouns can be omitted in defining clauses: "The film (that) I watched." Subject pronouns cannot be omitted.

opts: Is optional — removes without losing meaning
questions.hint: Defining = essential information. No commas. The sentence is unclear without it.

questions.text: "The Kite Runner, ___ is a novel by Hosseini, is Kamila's favourite." Fill in:

opts: Use commas and cannot be omitted
questions.correct: Use commas and cannot be omitted
questions.hint: Non-defining: always uses commas; cannot use "that"; adds extra info.

questions.text: "Amir, that studies engineering, won the prize" is correct.
questions.hint: Non-defining clauses cannot use "that." Correct: "Amir, who studies engineering, won the prize."

questions.text: "The film ___ I watched last night was excellent." Fill in (use the common neutral choice):
questions.hint: Defining clause — can use "that" or "which" for things. "that" is common in informal/neutral use.

questions.text: When can you omit "that/who" in a relative clause?
opts: When it is the subject of the clause
When it is the object of the clause
questions.correct: When it is the object of the clause
questions.hint: Object pronoun can be omitted in defining clauses: "The film (that) I watched." But not the subject: "The film that won." ✅

questions.text: WKU, ___ is in Uralsk, has a modern English programme.
Which is a correctly punctuated non-defining relative clause?
opts: Dr. Akhmetov who teaches English wrote a paper.
Dr. Akhmetov, who teaches English, wrote a paper.
Dr. Akhmetov, that teaches English, wrote a paper.
Dr. Akhmetov which teaches English wrote a paper.
questions.correct: Dr. Akhmetov, who teaches English, wrote a paper.
questions.hint: Non-defining: use commas; use "who" for people; never "that".

questions.text: In a defining clause, "that" can replace "who" or "which."
questions.hint: "that" can replace both "who" and "which" in defining relative clauses.

questions.text: Foundation, ___ Amir loves, is a classic science fiction series.
What type of film does Rustam want to see?

questions.text: Kamila says she will only go if it's a specific film she has chosen.
questions.hint: Statement 6: "She says she will go to any film that the group agrees on."

questions.hint: Statement 2: "She prefers films that have interesting characters and deep emotions."

questions.text: "Genre" in film and books refers to:
opts: A category or type of art, such as drama or comedy
questions.correct: A category or type of art, such as drama or comedy
questions.hint: "Genre" = a category of art or media, such as horror, romance, science fiction.
